race.name: West Coast Slugger
race.tagline: Port Alberni forest roads, waterfront views, steep walls, and enough isolation to make 45 mm tires feel sensible.

vitals.course_status_reason: The inaugural May 17, 2026 event is complete and the organizer has not announced its next date. The profile is live, but no dated race-specific plan is for sale.
vitals.registration: 2026 registration closed; next edition not announced
vitals.prize_purse: Awards and draw prizes; no cash purse published
vitals.aid_stations: One feed zone accessed multiple times by different routes
vitals.cutoff_time: Awards at 3:00 PM; no course-specific cutoff published
route_options: 2026 Impulso: 19.87 miles; the organizer page separately labels it 36.4 km, which is internally inconsistent

climate.description: The race bible requires riders to bring rain and wind layers, full-finger gloves, and warm headwear. Coastal rain and cool exposed forest roads are credible race constraints even though the organizer publishes no temperature range.

terrain.surface: The official race bible describes self-supported gravel and dirt roads around Port Alberni, open to logging and other authorized traffic. The organizer recommends 45-50 mm tires and warns about gates, bears, cougars, and limited cell coverage.
features: Sproat Lake and Alberni Inlet views

gravel_god_rating.score_note: The inaugural event had professional series support, three routes, a detailed race bible, remote forest terrain, and real waterfront character. One edition, no published gain, and no next date keep it at 57 and Tier 3.

biased_opinion.summary: West Coast Slugger is not a renamed Nanaimo Unpaved. The organizer introduced it as a new Port Alberni event in 2026, with longer forest-road options, lake and inlet views, steep wall climbs, logging traffic, and a race bible that treats self-sufficiency seriously.
weaknesses: Open logging roads and limited cell coverage
One organizer route conversion is internally inconsistent
biased_opinion.bottom_line: A real new Vancouver Island race worth adding to the database, but a future plan waits for a future date.

final_verdict.one_liner: A first-year island race with mature operations and genuinely remote terrain.
final_verdict.should_you_race: Yes when the organizer announces another edition—especially if you want long coastal forest roads and can handle self-supported logistics.
final_verdict.alternatives: For another active BC Gravel Series race, compare Forbidden Gravel.

logistics.airport: Access Vancouver Island by ferry or air, then drive to Port Alberni; verify the next venue before booking
logistics.lodging_strategy: Stay in Port Alberni close to packet pickup and the forest-road start; book only after a future date is official
logistics.food: The 2026 itinerary included a food truck from 11:00 AM to 3:00 PM; carry your own race nutrition between feed-zone passes
logistics.packet_pickup: 2026 Saturday pickup was at Jumping Slug Community Cyclery; Sunday pickup was at the Mosaic Log Sort
logistics.parking: The 2026 race bible designated parking at the Mosaic Log Sort

eligibility.status_note: The inaugural May 17, 2026 edition completed in Port Alberni. A next edition has not been announced.

history.founder: Panache Cycling Sports and BC Gravel Series
history.origin_story: BC Gravel Series introduced West Coast Slugger as a new Port Alberni event for its 2026 calendar.
notable_moments: The inaugural 2026 race offered 122.9 km, 76.4 km, and short-course options
history.reputation: A new but professionally operated Vancouver Island forest-road race.

course_description.character: A remote 122.9 km long course on coastal forest and logging roads with lake and inlet views, steep pitches, gates, wildlife, and limited cell coverage.

suffering_zones.label: Mosaic Log Sort
suffering_zones.desc: All distances start west on Stirling Arm Road before splitting into their forest-road loops.

suffering_zones.label: Waterfront Forest Roads
suffering_zones.desc: Long remote sectors around lakes and the Alberni Inlet combine scenery with limited support and open-road vigilance.

suffering_zones.label: The Walls
suffering_zones.desc: The organizer promises a couple of sheer walls; late-race gearing matters more than a missing headline elevation number suggests.

course_description.signature_challenge: Staying fueled, mechanically independent, and controlled on remote logging roads before the late steep pitches.

guide_variables.race_terrain: Remote coastal forest and logging roads with short steep walls
guide_variables.race_weather: Cool, wet, and windy coastal conditions are possible

non_negotiables.why: The inaugural 2026 race is complete and no next date is published.
The race bible warns of limited cell coverage and requires riders to carry repair, clothing, navigation, and nutrition gear.
The organizer explicitly recommends 45-50 mm tires to reduce pinch-flat and puncture risk.

migration_notes: Added as a newly verified relevant race under the user's standing add-grade-page rule
Kept separate from Nanaimo Unpaved because the organizer calls West Coast Slugger a new event
Elevation remains unknown rather than copied from unrelated Vancouver Island races
The official Impulso page has a miles-to-kilometres conflict; the profile flags it instead of silently choosing a conversion

logistics.explanation: Port Alberni requires island travel and a drive to an industrial forest venue, but the race bible gives clear packet, parking, and emergency instructions.

length.explanation: The official Esperto route is 76.37 miles, inside the rubric's 60-100-mile band.

technicality.explanation: Open logging roads, steep walls, gates, and a 45-50 mm tire recommendation create mixed technical demands without confirmed singletrack.

elevation.explanation: The organizer describes steep walls but publishes no total gain; a conservative 2 avoids inventing a number.

climate.explanation: The 2026 race bible required rain, wind, warm-head, and full-finger gear because coastal exposure is a material constraint.

altitude.explanation: The Port Alberni coastal setting does not create an altitude-training requirement.

adventure.explanation: Remote Port Alberni lake and inlet views, limited cell coverage, wildlife, and industrial forest roads make the course feel far from town.

prestige.explanation: BC Gravel Series affiliation is credible regionally, but the event has completed only one edition.

race_quality.explanation: A 14-page race bible, three routes, feed support, sweeps, medical staff, parking, packet pickup, and awards indicate professional operation.

experience.explanation: Port Alberni's forest and waterfront setting is materially more memorable than a generic regional road loop.

community.explanation: The BC Gravel Series has local partners and a community-cyclery pickup, but one edition cannot support a stronger culture claim.

field_depth.explanation: The organizer publishes no field size or evidence of a deep elite field for the 2026 edition.

value.explanation: The 3-route support package is substantial, but the official page does not preserve a final verifiable entry price.

expenses.explanation: Ferry or flight costs to Vancouver Island make the total trip moderate even for western-Canada riders.

topics.self_support: Remote forest-road nutrition, repair, and navigation
topics.climbing: Short steep wall pacing late in a long race

marketplace_variables.race_hook: 122.9 km of remote Vancouver Island gravel
marketplace_variables.race_hook_detail: A professionally operated Port Alberni race with waterfront forest roads, steep walls, and real self-support demands.
